title: 3PL Performance Benchmarks: How To Verify Your 3PL’s Numbers
summary: Learn which 3PL performance benchmarks matter and how to check your 3PL’s reported numbers against your own order and shipment data.
body_markdown:
In this article, learn about:


-


Why strong looking 3PL performance benchmarks can still hide missed orders


-


The five key performance indicators (KPIs) worth tracking and which ones you can check from your own records


-


How to measure 3PL performance by comparing account-specific reports with your own data


-


How an independent record from electronic data interchange (EDI) supports each review


Peak season puts 3PL relationships under a lot of pressure, and it is important that suppliers have a clear answer to whether their provider is performing adequately.


Published 3PL performance benchmarks give a starting point, but a benchmark helps only when you can check your own account against it. The[2027 Third-Party Logistics Study](https://www.mhlnews.com/technology-automation/news/55410240/ai-moving-to-operational-use-by-3pls) found that 97% of shippers and 98% of 3PLs call their relationships successful. The same study found that 70% of shippers are satisfied with their 3PL’s technology, while 94% of 3PLs believe their shippers are satisfied. A gap of 24% shows that a provider’s view of its service and its customers’ view can differ drastically.


## Why Can 3PL Performance Benchmarks Mislead You?


Benchmarks can mislead because a perfect order needs multiple things to go right. According to[APQC benchmarking data reported by IndustryWeek](https://www.industryweek.com/supply-chain/achieving-impossible-dream-perfect-order-performance) , a perfect order is one that arrives complete, on time, undamaged, and with the right paperwork. The median perfect order index is 90, so about one in 10 orders has some kind of failure. Organizations that reach 99% in each of the four areas still score only 96% overall.


The same math applies to the figures on a 3PL dashboard. When misses land on different orders, a 99% on-time rate and a 97% order accuracy rate multiply to about 96%, and that is before damage or paperwork errors are accounted for. Every figure can be accurate while the share of flawless orders is lower than any single figure suggests. A dashboard may also average results across the 3PL’s whole customer base, which means that each supplier’s account can look different.


## Which KPIs Belong on Your 3PL KPI Scorecard?


Five KPIs cover most of what a supplier needs to know:


-


Order accuracy


-


On-time shipping


-


Inventory accuracy


-


Perfect order rate


-


Cost per order


The table shows how each is calculated, the benchmark that providers commonly cite, and whether you can check it from your own records.


**KPI**


**How It Is Calculated**


**Commonly Cited Benchmark**


**Can You Verify It Yourself?**


Order accuracy


Error-free orders divided by total orders


Above 99%


Partly, by comparing advance ship notices (ASNs) and invoices with your purchase orders


On-time shipping


Orders shipped on time divided by total orders


Above 97%


Yes, by comparing each order date with the ship date in your records


Inventory accuracy


Physical count divided by system count


Above 99%


Mostly no, so request a cycle count or reconciliation report


Perfect order rate


On-time, complete, damage-free, and correctly documented rates multiplied together


About 90% (APQC median)


Partly, because retailer scorecards and chargebacks show late, short, or mislabeled orders


Cost per order


Total 3PL charges divided by orders shipped


No single benchmark; compare with your prior period


Yes, by dividing your total 3PL invoices by orders shipped


Benchmarks other than the APQC median come from guides that 3PL providers publish, so they are vendor-reported and not independently audited.


Two of the five KPIs can be checked entirely from your own data, two can be checked in part, and one depends mostly on the 3PL’s report. That split shows where independent records matter most.


## How To Measure 3PL Performance Against Your Own Data


The clearest picture comes from pairing the 3PL’s account-specific reports with records the supplier keeps.


### Request Account-Specific Reports


A summary across all of a provider’s customers shows how the provider does in general. One supplier’s results can look different. Suppliers can ask for reports filtered to their own account and time period. They can also ask how each metric is defined. An on-time rate that starts the clock at order placement gives a different result than one that starts at the end-of-day cutoff. The formula, the data source, the reporting schedule, and who can see the underlying data all belong in that conversation.


### Check Them Against Your Own Records


The steps below compare a 3PL’s report with records the supplier already holds:


1.


Pull the purchase orders, ASNs, and invoices for the review period.


1.


Compare each order date with the ship date to calculate your own on-time shipping rate.


1.


Match the quantities on your ASNs and invoices with the original purchase orders to estimate order accuracy.


1.


Review retailer chargebacks and customer complaints for the same orders to see where failures cluster.


1.


Divide your total 3PL invoices by orders shipped to calculate cost per order.


1.


Request a cycle count or reconciliation report and compare it with your own inventory records.


1.


Put your figures next to the 3PL’s report and ask about any gap that definitions can’t explain.


These checks need the supplier’s own record of orders, shipments, and invoices, not just the 3PL’s copy. Suppliers typically build that record with EDI systems that exchange documents with retailers automatically. In a[2020 SPS survey](https://spscommerce.com/blog/3pl-study-finds-accurate-data-key-to-shipping-accuracy) of nearly 200 3PLs, 75% said automation means fewer errors and 73% said it improves order accuracy. Those figures are providers’ own views and are six years old. They indicate a direction and do not prove a result.


Two SPS customers show what owning the data flow looks like on each side of the relationship.[True Brands](https://www.spscommerce.com/resources/case-study-true-brands/) , a supplier of beverage accessories, added a 3PL for its Walmart business and automated order flow to the provider and to more than 70 retailers. The company reports hands-free fulfillment of more than $5 million in Walmart orders a year, along with fewer chargebacks.[Symbia Logistics](https://www.spscommerce.com/resources/symbia-logistics-deposco/) , a family-owned 3PL, took the provider’s side. It worked with SPS Commerce and Deposco to handle EDI errors, customer onboarding, and system testing, and it gained visibility into its customers’ data.


## How Often Should You Run a 3PL Performance Review?


Quarterly is the minimum, and monthly reviews fit suppliers with higher order volume. Each review should use the same KPIs and the same definitions, because a trend says more than a single month. A hypothetical order accuracy rate that slips from 99.5% to 99.0% to 98.5% across three months may look acceptable each time and still signal a developing problem.


An extra review during peak season shows how a 3PL performs under its heaviest load. Whatever the schedule, each review is the moment to place the 3PL’s report beside your own records and ask about any difference.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is a good order accuracy rate for a 3PL?


Providers commonly cite 99% or higher, and some cite 99.5% or more. Those figures are vendor-reported, so they work best as a reference point. A rate that stays below 99% across several months is worth raising with the 3PL.


### Can I verify my 3PL’s numbers without a logistics analyst?


For two of the five KPIs, yes. On-time shipping and cost per order can be calculated from your own order, shipment, and invoice records. The others need more data or a report from the 3PL, such as a cycle count.


### Is a perfect order rate better than tracking each KPI separately?


A perfect order rate shows what customers actually received, because a failure in any one dimension counts against the whole order. It also draws on data from several sources, so tracking the individual KPIs alongside it helps show where failures start.


### What should I do if my 3PL misses its targets?


Suppliers typically ask for a written explanation of the cause and a plan to fix it, then watch whether the miss repeats. A single miss can come from a carrier disruption or a volume spike, while repeated misses point to a process problem.
